Method of Attack: Malware spreads via a booby-trapped file named 'driversUpdate.exe' to infect users' computers
Malware queries a hard-coded Twitter account for commands to start and stop DDoS attacks
Commands include launching DDoS attacks, stopping attacks, downloading and executing files, and executing CLI commands
DDoS attacks are launched from infected users' computers
Malware creates hidden Windows forms to simulate user clicks to start attacks
Impacted Systems: Windows PCs infected by the malware
Attack Vector: Booby-trapped executable file 'driversUpdate.exe' distributed to users
